questions.question: You had 5 stickers. Now you have 8 stickers. What changed?
questions.explain: You started with 5 and now have 8, so 3 were added. Watch out: 8 is the new total, not the change.

questions.question: You had 9 apples. Now you have 6 apples. What changed?
questions.explain: You started with 9 and now have 6, so 3 were taken away. The change is the difference between the two numbers, not the number you end with.

questions.question: You had 4 blocks. Now you have 12 blocks. What changed?
questions.explain: You started with 4 and now have 12, so 8 were added. Do not pick the starting number or the ending number as the change.

questions.question: You had 15 crayons. Now you have 11 crayons. What changed?
questions.explain: You started with 15 and now have 11, so 4 were taken away. 11 is how many you have now, not how many changed.

questions.question: Mia had 7 shells on her beach blanket. Now she has 11 shells. What changed?
questions.explain: Mia went from 7 to 11, so 4 were added. Count the difference between the two numbers to find the change.

questions.question: Sam had 10 marbles. Now he has 7 marbles. What changed?
questions.explain: Sam went from 10 to 7, so 3 were taken away. He lost marbles, so it is fewer, not more.

questions.question: There were 6 ducks in the pond. Now there are 14 ducks. What changed?
questions.explain: The ducks went from 6 to 14, so 8 were added. The change is the difference, not the number you start with or end with.

questions.question: Lily had 13 cookies. Now she has 5 cookies. What changed?
questions.explain: Lily went from 13 to 5, so 8 were taken away. She ate them, so it is fewer, not more.

questions.question: A tank had 7 fish, then 3 left and 6 came back. Now there are 10 fish. How did the total change?
questions.explain: Start with 7, end with 10, so the change is 3 more. Compare the first number and the last number; you do not just pick one event.

questions.question: Zoe had 12 pebbles, gave 5 away, and a bird dropped 8. Now she has 15. What changed from the start?
questions.explain: Zoe started with 12 and ended with 15, so the change is 3 more. Always compare the very first number and the very last number.

questions.question: Ben had 4 cubes, added some, and now has 9. His mom says, 'You added 9 cubes!' What is her mistake?
options: She counted the cubes one more time
She said taken away instead of added
She gave the total, not the change
She said there were fewer, not more
questions.explain: The real change is 9 minus 4, which is 5. Mom gave the new total instead of the change.

questions.question: Max had 16 gummy bears, ate some, and his brother gave him 3 more. Now he has 14. How many did Max eat?
questions.explain: Max started with 16, got 3 more, and ended with 14. So he ate 16 plus 3 minus 14, which is 5. Do not pick the number he ended with.
